title: Observability, Evaluation & Cost
description: Study service and quality telemetry, offline and online evaluation, cost attribution and budgets, and load testing realistic workloads. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Service and quality telemetry
lessons.description: Define an alert for quality regression alongside service availability.
lessons.conceptOverview: Track latency, errors, saturation and task-quality signals separately. Operational health does not prove answer correctness; connect sampled quality reviews to model and data versions.

lessons.title: Offline and online evaluation
lessons.description: Plan an experiment with language-level quality gates.
lessons.conceptOverview: Offline fixtures enable reproducible comparisons; online experiments reveal real traffic behavior. Use guardrails and segmented analysis so a global average does not hide harm to a smaller user group.
lessons.whyItMatters: Rollout decisions should inspect important traffic segments.

lessons.title: Cost attribution and budgets
lessons.description: Define cost per attempted task and per successful task.
lessons.conceptOverview: Attribute preprocessing, storage, retrieval and generation costs to workloads or tenants. Include retries and failed jobs; successful-request cost alone understates operational spend.
lessons.whyItMatters: Cost accounting must include failed and repeated work.

lessons.title: Load testing realistic workloads
lessons.description: Build a workload mix with warm and cold paths and long outputs.
lessons.conceptOverview: Load tests need realistic input sizes, output lengths, cache hit rates and burst patterns. Short synthetic requests can overestimate capacity for long-context production workloads.
lessons.whyItMatters: Capacity estimates depend on representative workload distributions.
